gloss: to be fed up; to be sick and tired of; to be bored stiff

definitions.gloss: to be fed up; to be sick and tired of; to be weary of
definitions.explanation: To feel exhausted patience or strong boredom with something repetitive, tedious, or irritating.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{会議|かいぎ}にうんざりした。
examples.english: I was fed up with the long meeting.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{自慢話|じまんばなし}にはうんざりさせられる。
examples.english: His bragging really makes me sick and tired.

notes:
An onomatopoeic expression conveying strong weariness or boredom. Stronger than {飽|あ}きる and carries more exhaustion than {嫌|いや}になる. Often used when patience has been completely worn out.

USAGE:
Can be used as an adverb (うんざりする), a na-adjective-like form (うんざりだ), or in a causative pattern (うんざりさせる). The source of frustration is marked by に: Xにうんざりする.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- Xにうんざりする: to be fed up with X
- うんざりするほど: to the point of being sick of it
- うんざりさせる: to make someone fed up
- うんざりした{顔|かお}: a fed-up expression

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {嫌|いや}になる: to become fed up — similar but slightly milder
- {飽|あ}き{飽|あ}きする: to be completely bored — emphasizes extreme tedium
- げんなりする: to feel disheartened — similar weariness but with more deflation than irritation

cross_references.label: shrinking back, being fed up, weariness
